title: Your age was never one number.
deck: Risk of dying, vs people with no organs aging early

_provenance.paper: doi:10.1038_s41591-025-03798-1 · Oh et al. 2025, Nat Med · prospective cohort, plasma proteomics (2,916 proteins), 11 organ-age estimates, UK Biobank n=44,498, 2-17y follow-up
_provenance.axis: x = count of biologically aged organs (of 11 estimated). The paper bins 2-4 / 5-7 / 8+; points sit at bin midpoints (3, 6) with the open 8+ bin plotted at its FLOOR (8) — conservative, never overstating. 'Aged organ' = age-gap z-score > 1.5 in that organ's model (full text, Methods); translated on the frame as 'aging early'.
_provenance.reference: 'Normal agers' (full text: multi-organ agers tested against normal agers) — HR 1.00 by definition; the (0, 1.0, 'normal aging') point is the comparator, not a reported estimate

claims.quote: Accrual of aged organs progressively increased mortality risk (2-4 aged organs, HR = 2.3

_provenance.copy_grounding: 'IT STACKS / Every aged organ raises it' + 'IT ACCELERATES / The jumps get bigger' ← 'Accrual of aged organs progressively increased mortality risk' and the reported sequence (+1.3, +2.2, +3.8 between bins). '11' ← 'the biological age of 11 organs'. 'aging early' ← extreme-ager definition (z > 1.5).
_provenance.reveal_test: Headline names the one-age belief and withholds the replacement; the counter climbing through organ counts and the risk curve compounding supply it, with 8.3× as the completion payoff. 'IT STACKS' is on screen from t≈0.2s.
_provenance.honesty: Rising curve — first one in the series; the area fill grows with risk, so motion = the bad news arriving, which is the honest shape of this claim. Segments between markers are interpolation per the template contract; no 0-1 organ bin is reported, and no point is drawn there. The youthful-organ protection trio (c6-c8: HR 0.60/0.58/0.44) is caption material — the hopeful flip, never a second curve.
